title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of the ILO constituents to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: In April 2020, the Ministry of Labour, in consultation with social partners, developed and launched an apprenticeship programme and curriculum for the hotel sector focusing on four occupations: food production; front office; food and beverages services; housekeeping and laundry. The apprenticeship program, implemented through Uganda Hotel Owners Association, has recruited an initial cohort of 116 apprentices and mobilized 40 private sector hotels to train the apprentices and undertaken workplace readiness inspection of the participating hotels to ensure the workplaces are safe for them. The programme is designed to run for a 12-month period with 3 months training at the college and 9 month training at the workplace. Between April to September 2020, with support from government of Netherlands, ILO provided financial and technical support (through external collaborators and ILO staff technical inputs) to tripartite partners including Federation of Uganda Employers (FUE), National Organization of Trade Unions (NOTU), Ministry of Labour (MGLSD), Ministry of Education (MoE), the Uganda Hotel Owners' Association (UHOA) and the Uganda Hotel and Tourism Training Institute (UHTTI), to design apprenticeship programme and curriculum for the four hotel sector occupations.

description.narrative:
In June 2020, the Government designed and piloted an Urban Cash for Work Programme (UCWP), implemented by the Ministry of Labour in the Rural District of Arua, targetting 4,195 informal sector workers. The programme is based on the National Guidelines for the Planning, Design and Implementation of Labour-Intensive Public Works (LIPW) in Uganda. The purpose of the UCWP is to mitigate the income shocks encountered by some of the households in rural Arua District, affected as a result of the various measures instituted by Government to contain the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic.
During 2020 and 2021, the Government, in consultation with constituents and under the leadership of Ministry of Labour, developed a Jobs and Livelihoods Integrated Response Plan (JLIRP) for Refugees and Host Communities. The National Steering Committee (chaired by the Ministry of Labour) was established and launched in April 2021. Its purpose is to provide support to the government to integrate the JLIRP into the District Development Plans of the 13 rural districts that host refugees. The plan is designed to run for five years, from June 2020 – June 2025 in the refugee hosting districts. Between June and August 2020, with support from the government of Netherlands, ILO provided Technical Assistance to Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development (MGLSD) in the design of the Urban Cash for Work Programme (UCWP). This ILO technical support involved recruitments of External Collaborators who worked with the ministry in the design of the programme
In November 2020, following the finalisation of the design of the UCWP, ILO provided support to the MGLSD to implement pilot UCWP in Arua City, targeting 4,195 people affected by the effects of COVID-19 restrictions to curb its spread.
In August 2020 and April 2021, with support from the government of Netherlands, ILO provided technical assistance, to Office of the Prime Minister (responsible for Refugees), Ministry of Labour, and Employers, strengthening their capacity through ITCILO Courses on Decent Work for Refugees and Market Based Livelihoods Programming for refugees and host communities. This ILO technical assistance targeted the government teams from Ministry of Labour and Office of the Prime Minister as teams that led the development of the Jobs and Livelihoods Integrated Response Plan for refugees and host communities.
Between June and August, with the support from the Government of Netherlands, the ILO provided additional technical support to MGLSD, National Planning Authority and 13 refugee-hosting districts of Uganda. This Technical assistance was aimed at providing external collaborators to work with social partners to intergrate the JLIRP into the district development plans of the 13 refugee hostibg districts; Madi Okollo, Terego, Adjumani, Kikuube, Yumbe, Obongi, Kiryandongo, Kyegegwa, Isingiro, Lamwo, Kampala, Kamwenge, and Koboko.

Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises to adopt new business models, technology and techniques to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
Through various interventions, Business Development Service Providers Network (a network of trainers in ILO Enterprise tools of SIYB and GET Ahead) has provided business development training to 590 micro-enterprises owned (187 women owned enterprises and 293 male owned micro enterprises) by refugees and host community members. The Federation of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises in Uganda (FSME), with ILO technical and financial support has also provided 200 micro SME's with small business grants to meet their short -term cash needs and to keep the business operational. These entrepreneurs already engaged in various sectors, for example restaurants, bars, retail trade and agribusinesses.
In August 2021, three District Local Governments i.e. Arua, Madi-Okollo and Terego signed Memorandums of Understanding (MoU's) with the Private Sector to work together in addressing key bottlenecks in two value chains (e.g. cassava and sesame) while working through lead enterprises to provide livelihoods and economic opportunities for rural refugees and host communities that are participating in these value chains. 10 lead enterprises in these two values chains have been provided with matching grants of US$ 30,000 each, to invest in development and growth of their enterprises, while providing forward and back ward linkages that will create opportunities for 5,000 refugees and host communities participated in the various stages of the value chains. This will increase their economic and livelihoods capabilities and opportunities. With support of the Dutch government, in 2020 the ILO facilitated technical Training of 39 "Start and Improve your Business" (SIYB) trainers and certified them to deliver demand-driven entrepreneurship skills to refugees and host communities. A total of 39 SIYB candidate trainers who are members of a network of providers of business development services, were supported to conduct their initial training of entrepreneurs. Until September 2021, they trained 390 entrepreneurs from host community members and refugees.
